name: Dugout canoe
status: Quick test. Shaped, cleaned and surfaced as a standard 3D model. Not yet in Skyrim's model format and not in the game.
summary: A single hollowed cypress log, 4.5 m long. The first thing made under owner call #93, to try the measure-and-look loop end to end and to give the asset explorer something real to show.

need.why: Nothing like it is held. Searched 28,880 model files and 40,968 catalogue records by record name, display name and model path for dugout, canoe, pirogue, punt and raft: no hit. Every boat model we hold was then looked at one at a time: King of the Murkmire's are plank river boats about 10 m long, the rest are rowboats, jolly boats and longboats. The nearest held shapes are rotted logs, which are not hulls.
need.lore: Riverback country is "a drowned marsh navigable by small rafts, canoes, and little else"; personal rafts are "the old ways" and the default vehicle (story/lore/topics/material-culture.md, lines 95 to 106).
need.use: Moored at the 22 raft-master boat stops, and at fishing camps and creek landings. A static: boarding is a line of dialogue that fast-travels, so it needs no seat.

brief.material: one swamp cypress log, hewn with an adze
brief.no: paint, metal, ornament, rope or any other thin part
brief.text: 4.5 m long, 0.7 m wide; one swamp cypress log, hewn with an adze. None of: paint, metal, ornament, rope or any other thin part.

fees.note: Fal's list prices for the options used, read on 24 November 2026 from each model's Fal page; Fal's request history shows no charge per request, so these are not from a bill.

stages.name: 1. Reference images
stages.did: Three reference images from one written brief (Fal, Nano Banana 2.1), plain grey background, three-quarter view from above so the hollow and one full side show.
stages.looked: All three read as a dugout. The second was chosen: the cleanest outline, blunt ends, the hollow fully visible. Each carried a rope as the brief asked, and that turned out to be the mistake (next stage).
stages.decision: After the first generation the rope was edited out of the chosen image and nothing else changed. Lesson for the brief: no rope, cord or other thin part in a reference; thin parts are added by hand afterwards.
images: Reference 1: rope hangs down the side
Reference 3: most character, but a hanging rope and a soft shadow
Reference 2 with the rope edited out: the image the kept model was made from
stages.prompt: Game asset reference photo of a single dugout canoe carved from one swamp cypress log, about 4.5 metres long and 0.7 metres wide, empty, no people, no paddle, no water. Blunt rounded bow and stern, thick walls about 5 cm, the inside hollowed with visible adze chop marks, outside bark stripped, a shallow carved notch at the bow with one loop of frayed plant-fibre rope tied through it. Old, dark, weathered wet wood, grey-brown, a little green algae near the waterline, muted desaturated colours, worn edges, no ornament, no paint, no metal. Three-quarter view from slightly above so the whole hollow interior and one full side are visible, the entire canoe inside the frame with margin. Flat even diffuse studio lighting with no hard shadows and no highlights, plain mid-grey seamless background, nothing else in the picture.

stages.name: 2. Generation, first try
stages.did: The chosen image went to two generators at once, Tripo P2 and Tripo H3.1, each asked for at most 20,000 triangles with a detailed texture.
stages.looked: Both are plainly a dugout. On both, the rope became lumps of stray geometry: a yellow tangle at the bow on P2, and on H3.1 one lump at the bow and another in the middle of the floor. H3.1 also drew panel lines across the floor that are not in the reference.
stages.decision: Thrown away. The numbers agreed with the eye: P2 came back in 287 separate pieces with 483 edges shared by more than two faces. Regenerate from a reference with no rope.
images: Tripo P2, first try, six fixed views
Tripo H3.1, first try, six fixed views

stages.name: 3. Generation, second try
stages.did: The same two generators, from the rope-free image.
stages.looked: No stray lumps on either. P2 gives a slim, even boat shape with a mottled, pebbly surface that does not read as wood. H3.1 gives a chunkier hewn log with a flat-cut stern, a cracked rim and a surface that does read as carved wood. It came back turned at an angle in its own frame, which the next stage corrects.
stages.decision: H3.1 kept: one closed piece with no open or shared edges, and the better look. P2 kept beside it as the alternative, since its hull is the more boat-like.
images: Tripo P2, second try: the alternative

stages.name: 4. Shaping
stages.did: Turned to its own long axis, found from the real vertices; set upright by which side is the open one; scaled so the length is 4.5 m; stood on the ground with its middle at the origin. The hull was then brought to the brief's beam: the generation was 1.18 m across at 4.5 m long, so its cross-section (width and depth together) was scaled to 0.7 m across, its length kept (tobrief.py).
stages.looked: Upright, level, reads as a hewn dugout from all six views. The hole at the bow survives.
stages.decision: Kept at 4.5 m by 0.7 m, 0.39 m deep, as the brief asks.

stages.name: 5. Clean-up
stages.did: Checked for stray vertices, loose pieces, holes and bad edges (none on this model), then cut the triangle count while keeping the texture layout.
stages.looked: At 4,000 triangles the rim turns visibly angular in the three-quarter view. At 8,000 the six views are hard to tell from the 19,978-triangle original.
stages.decision: 4,000 undone as too rough; 8,000 kept. For scale, the 29 m Imperial ship we hold is 12,324 triangles, so 8,000 is heavy for a 4.5 m boat. Getting lower without the angular rim means rebuilding the rim by hand, which the quick test did not do.

stages.name: 6. Surface
stages.did: Three surfaces on the same cleaned shape. A: the generator's own texture, one picture for the whole boat. B: a repeating hewn-cypress material made once from a Fal swatch, wrapped on by box projection from the real face normals at 1,280 pixels per metre, grain along the hull. C: the same material, with shading and wear carried as vertex colour sampled from the generator's texture, which is Skyrim's own way to darken and tint.

measured.A_pixels_per_metre: about 260 (4,096 px over 15.7 m2 of surface, if the layout were fully used)
measured.ranges_measured_from_the_game: not yet: no level 0 sheet exists

stages.looked: A has the most character: a dark hollow, a pale worn rim, cracks, a green stain. B reads as wood with the grain running the right way, but flat and pale, and it loses the rim, the cracks and the stain. The first attempt at B was worse, because the material was made to repeat by mirroring and showed kaleidoscope patterns; it was remade by cross-fading its edges into its own middle. C gets the dark hollow and underside back and sits between the two.
stages.decision: Not settled, and it bears on the plan. The shared material gives sharpness and sameness across a set; the generated texture gives the character. On this object the generated texture looks better. C suggests the way through: shared material for the surface, the generation's shading carried on top. Look at all three and say which direction you want.
images: C: shared material with shading as vertex colour

stages.name: 7. Into the game
stages.did: Nothing yet. This is the proof in the proposal, not part of the quick test.
stages.decision: Still owed: Skyrim's model format; a collision shape taken from the real hull so a player can stand in it; the colour and brightness ranges measured from the game; a distant-view model; placing it at a boat stop; your look in game.

stages.name: Cost experiment: cheaper generators
stages.did: The same reference image went once to each cheaper route on Fal, and to Meshy 7.1. Every result is scaled to the brief (tobrief.py) before it is shown, so all of them stand in true metres beside the 1.8 m person.

measured.prices: Prices are Fal's list prices, not from a bill.
measured.seconds: The generator's own reported time where it reports one; Trellis 2, Hunyuan and Tripo do not report it.

stages.looked: Each result was looked at from six fixed views; the one-line note per route is in the table.
stages.decision: The owner's pick is Tripo H3.1: the best shape and the best texture of all three things. The rest are listed under 'Other generators tried', ranked.

Idol max turbo, $0.10: kept after clean-up
Tripo H3.1 bare + our material, $0.20: kept

routes.look: Plainly the dugout: blunt ends, the mooring holes, a clean hollow, dark weathered wood with a green stain. Only 3,258 triangles, one closed piece; the texture is softer than H3.1 but right in colour. Usable as it comes after scaling.
Reads well and keeps the outline; wood with grey weathering and moss, a little lumpy along the rim. One closed piece, 29,366 triangles.
Right shape, one closed piece, but the texture is a flat brown with almost no grain or wear; it would want our shared material on top.
Rejected before it ran: the reference image was 1,204 KB and this route takes at most 950 KB. Nothing came back.
Reads as a dugout but the bow came out pointed (the reference is blunt), the texture is blurred, and there are 10 small loose pieces to remove; it also arrived turned on a diagonal.
Asked for no texture, it still came back painted: a good closed hull of 19,738 triangles in the right proportions, but scratchy marks like writing in the hollow. Kept for its shape.
The same bare hull wrapped in our hewn-cypress material: reads as one hewn log, even and sharp, but flat, with none of the generated wear.
A clean, symmetrical hull; smoother and greyer than H3.1 with fainter adze marks. Six pieces (five specks). Three times H3.1's price.
